title: saml provisioning latency causes dual-role states and audit mismatch
creator: Maya Chen
description: Several enterprise customers reported intermittent permission denials followed by later over-permissioned access after SSO login during peak provisioning windows. Root cause appears to be a race between our SAML provisioning worker and the session/role-apply path: when assertion handling is delayed (SAML IdP retries / network flaps), a user can sign in and be given a temporary minimal session (deny-by-default) while a late provisioning callback applies a stale role set that includes broader privileges. Audit records are either missing the assertion correlation or show two separate session_ids, making forensic reviews difficult. This ticket tracks the investigation, fix, and rollout to ensure atomic role application and reliable audit linkage.
reproduction_steps: 1) Configure SAML IdP with large group membership (~200 groups) and enable delayed assertion delivery (simulate network 150-400ms extra latency).
2) Trigger user login during a rolling role-sync deploy to increase contention on the provisioning queue.

3) Observe that frontend issues initial session with default-deny, while async provisioner later applies roles tied to a different session_id, resulting in transient denial then sudden permission grant.
4) Check audit logs: missing assertion_id or mismatched session identifiers between auth and role-apply events.
proposed_fix: 1) Correlate SAML assertion_uuid with session_id at creation and persist in the short-lived provisioning token.
2) Implement an atomic role-apply step that locks the session row (DB optimistic lock -> compare-and-swap) so role mutations are idempotent and ordered relative to session creation.
3) Backfill patch: scan audit events for assertion_uuid collisions and annotate affected sessions for retrospective alerts and customer notifications.
4) Add a short-term mitigation: hold initial session activation for up to 250ms if provisioning for that user is pending (configurable flag behind feature gate).
rollout_plan: Canary: deploy role-apply lock and assertion_uuid persistence to ci-dedicated and 10% of hosted region traffic for 48h.
Monitor for false negatives (users seeing delays) and false positives (increased 500s).
If stable, ramp to 50% for 24h, then 100% and run backfill job during a low-traffic window.
Customer notifications: email affected enterprise tenants with remediation timeline; provide temporary support playbook for escalations.
qa_checks: Unit tests for assertion_uuid propagation and idempotent role-apply.
Integration test that simulates delayed SAML assertions and validates only a single session transition in audit logs.
Load test with synthetic SAML spikes to verify no new contention introduced by session locking under 2k RPS.
Manual verification with 3 enterprise test tenants and explicit audit trail review.
monitoring_and_alerts: Alert: >5 auth->role mismatches per minute for a tenant => pager (oncall-sre).
Dashboard: session_lifecycle_stream showing assertion_uuid, session_id, role_events correlated.
